ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py:435](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L435), [dynamic_management.py:450](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L450), and [dynamic_management.py:477](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L477) key Role Assignment state only by `model_id`, but `assign()` never checks that IDs are unique. Two distinct `ModelSpec`s with the same ID silently overwrite each other in `capability_scores`, `role_map`, and `_failure_history`. I verified this with three input models `('dup', 'dup', 'x')`: `len(models) == 3`, but the returned `role_map` and failure-history table both had length 2.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Fail fast in `assign()` if `model_id`s are not unique. The same invariant should also be enforced in `DynamicManager.__init__` so downstream components do not inherit a collapsed identity map.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py:505](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L505) always seeds `new_map` with the locked PM, while [dynamic_management.py:507](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L507) only filters non-PM IDs from `active_models`. If the caller passes an active set that excludes the PM, `reassign()` resurrects that inactive PM anyway. I verified this directly: `ra.reassign(1, {'a', 'b'})` returned `{'pm': PM, 'a': COL, 'b': PAR}`. That violates the method’s own `active_models` contract and can leave role state inconsistent with liveness state.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate that `pm_model_id` is present in `active_models` before building `new_map`. If it is missing, raise or return an explicit failure state rather than manufacturing a role map with an inactive PM.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_RA_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.67  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py:507](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L507) builds `remaining_ids` from a `set`, and [dynamic_management.py:539](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L539) chooses `best_col_id` with `max()` on score alone. Unlike initial assignment, `reassign()` never applies `_tie_break_key()`. When the current COL is inactive and two challengers tie, the winner depends on hash/set iteration order rather than a declared rule. I verified this by rerunning the same scenario with different `PYTHONHASHSEED`s: one run promoted `a1`, another promoted `b2`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Reuse the initial deterministic ranking rule in `reassign()`, for example by sorting candidates on `(adjusted_score, _tie_break_key(model), model_id)` and picking the first.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py:473](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L473) stores `capability_scores` once during initial assignment, but [dynamic_management.py:515](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L515) recomputes adjusted COL scores during `reassign()` without writing them back, and [dynamic_management.py:581](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L581) continues to serve the stale table via `get_ordering()`. I verified this with two recorded failures on the current COL: `role_map` switched to `par1` as COL, while `get_ordering(Role.COL)` still reported `col0` ahead of `par1`. The object’s public state becomes self-contradictory after reassignment.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either recompute and persist current scores/orderings on each reassignment, or explicitly scope `capability_scores` to “initial scores” and add a separate API for the live adjusted ordering.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py:235](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L235) documents `CapabilityFingerprint` as bounded schema data, but there is no validation on `CapabilityFingerprint` or `ModelSpec`, and [dynamic_management.py:393](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L393) claims `_capability_score()` returns a scalar in `[0, 1]`. That claim is false for accepted inputs today. I verified that a model with `D_decay = -0.1` produced a PM score of `1.15`. Invalid fingerprints therefore distort ordering instead of being rejected.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `__post_init__` validation to `CapabilityFingerprint` for finite numeric values and the intended domain bounds, and reject NaN/inf/out-of-range inputs before normalization or scoring.
